s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
key_facts: Hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia in March 2020
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS
Relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye
Mild anterior chamber inflammation and noticeable pupillary edema
2 peripapillary hemorrhages and mild vitreous inflammation
Retinal vessel narrowing in the inferior retina
Normal complete blood cell counts and serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Normal cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2 and severe bilateral pneumonia

shortlist.label: Optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision in the right eye

shortlist.label: Retinal vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluorescein leakage from retinal venules and retinal vessel narrowing in the inferior retina

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Very weakly positive IgG for VZV and ocular involvement

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Very weakly positive IgG for CMV and severe immunocompromised state suggested by severe bilateral pneumonia

raw.rationale: The patient's recent close contact with a fatal case and positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, along with the development of severe bilateral pneumonia and subsequent ocular symptoms, strongly support COVID-19 as the underlying cause.

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: While the patient exhibits some symptoms consistent with optic neuritis, such as blurred vision and relative afferent pupil defect, the broader clinical context and positive SARS-CoV-2 test point towards COVID-19 as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: The presence of retinal vessel narrowing and fluorescein leakage from retinal venules could suggest retinal vasculitis, but these findings are also compatible with the ocular manifestations of COVID-19.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
rejected.why: The very weakly positive IgG for VZV does not strongly support an active VZV infection, and the clinical presentation is more consistent with COVID-19.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
rejected.why: The very weakly positive IgG for CMV, similar to VZV, does not strongly support an active CMV infection, and the clinical context points more towards complications associated with COVID-19.
